scope: standalone fixed-motor intake capture and free handoff on the authoritative ramp
supersedes: schema_version 1 (flat frictionless ground datum). Every number downstream of the exit vector in that revision is invalidated.

frame_mapping.cad_ground_frame: Option A: origin at the chassis plate centre, z=0 at the court, +X forward
frame_mapping.base_link_frame: xacro_z = cad_z - 0.045; xacro_x = cad_x + packaging shift

frozen_contact_sequence.note: frozen CAD geometry only; asserted by tests/test_intake_frame_alignment.py

bridge_under_z_source_conflict_m.note: reported, not silently reconciled; authority 1 owns bridge geometry

motor_model.law: linear torque-speed and torque-current bounded model

sensitivity_bounds.ball_ramp_friction_bound_rationale: dry tennis felt on a smooth rigid printed/plywood sheet; 0.20 covers a slick surface and 0.60 a rough unfinished one
sensitivity_bounds.tyre_law: linear radial spring in series with calibrated ball law

approach_speed.why_it_is_reported: The frozen ramp lip reaches a court-resting ball 48.6 mm before the first centred wheel contact (see ground_profile.frozen_contact_sequence), so the ball must cross the wedge on its own momentum. Approach speed is therefore a first-order variable, not a nuisance parameter. It is a COMMANDED operating value, not an unmeasured coefficient.

ramp_effect.note: The flat-ground column is the INVALID legacy datum, reproduced only so the change can be quantified. Every flat-ground number in the previous report is withdrawn.

basket_on_base.definition: worst-case intersection over every valid trial: the ball bottom must pass above the rim top at that rearward distance

population_definitions.centred_HIGH: y=0 entries, HIGH wheel-speed command, all unmeasured bounds
population_definitions.centred_NOMINAL: y=0 entries, NOMINAL wheel-speed command, all unmeasured bounds
population_definitions.centred_LOW: y=0 entries, LOW wheel-speed command, all unmeasured bounds
population_definitions.centred_entries_all_bounds: y=0 entries, all three wheel-speed commands
population_definitions.all_valid_entries: every valid entry including lateral offsets

low_rim_versus_rebound_conflict.statement: A low rim is required for the ball to clear it, while a deep energy-absorbing entry is required to stop rebound escape. These pull in opposite directions and are NOT resolved here; no basket geometry is designed in this task.

gazebo_campaign.scope: Gazebo owns ramp wedge/plough dynamics with ground friction, cheek centering, capture half-width, jam/reject modes and 6-DOF multi-contact. Wheel droop, torque and current are NOT measurable here (ideal velocity source) and are not reported.

cross_validation.compared_case: centred ball, authoritative ramp, same approach speeds
cross_validation.tolerance: qualitative on the capture/plough mechanism at each approach speed. Exit velocity is NOT cross-compared: Gazebo uses rigid contact with kp/kd conditioning and does not own that quantity.
cross_validation.disagreement: Above the plough threshold the two instruments differ: the reduced-order solver transports a centred ball at 0.80 m/s, Gazebo reaches the wheel bite and rejects it. The gap is narrow — both put the ball at the front face of the nip — and it is REPORTED, NOT TUNED AWAY. Candidate causes, none of which may be adjusted to close it: the two contact laws at the 1.5 mm lip (calibrated ball law vs rigid kp/kd), the solver's 2-contact reduction versus 6-DOF multi-contact, and the absence of tyre compliance in the Gazebo wheel. Settling it needs the physical ramp-lip test, not a model change.

gazebo_campaign.markdown:
**S1 — ramp dynamics (Phase 3: wheels + ramp, no cheeks), centred ball.**
The nip mid-plane sits at base_link x = 370 mm and the ramp
front lip at 420 mm. `minimum ball x` is how far the ball
ever got toward the nip; `advance` is how far it was pushed forward in the world.

`REJECTED_AT_NIP` means the ball reached the wheel bite and was spat out again.
`Advance` saturates at the court net (world x=0), so it is a floor, not the
distance the ball would have travelled on an open court.

**Cross-validation gate.** qualitative on the capture/plough mechanism at each approach speed. Exit velocity is NOT cross-compared: Gazebo uses rigid contact with kp/kd conditioning and does not own that quantity.
Solver centred capture by approach speed: {"0.35": false, "0.60": false, "0.80": true}.
Gazebo centred capture by approach speed: {"0.35": false, "0.60": false, "0.80": false}.
`CROSS_INSTRUMENT_AGREEMENT = AGREE_ON_PLOUGH_AT_ROUTE_SPEEDS`.
Above the plough threshold the two instruments differ: the reduced-order solver transports a centred ball at 0.80 m/s, Gazebo reaches the wheel bite and rejects it. The gap is narrow — both put the ball at the front face of the nip — and it is REPORTED, NOT TUNED AWAY. Candidate causes, none of which may be adjusted to close it: the two contact laws at the 1.5 mm lip (calibrated ball law vs rigid kp/kd), the solver's 2-contact reduction versus 6-DOF multi-contact, and the absence of tyre compliance in the Gazebo wheel. Settling it needs the physical ramp-lip test, not a model change.

stop_reasons: STOP CONDITION (task section 14): on the authoritative ramp the ball is PLOUGHED AHEAD and never reaches the nip at the collection route's commanded speeds (0.35 m/s nominal, 0.60 m/s maximum). Capture first appears at 0.675 m/s and is bound-wide from 0.775 m/s.
nonzero lateral entries are not reliable across the full bounded friction, ramp-friction and tyre-compliance matrix
tyre compliance, felt/tread friction and ball-to-ramp friction remain physically unmeasured

STOP CONDITION (task section 14): the Gazebo campaign captured no ball at any tested approach speed, tread friction or lateral offset. S2-S5 therefore have nothing to measure and stay gated: capture half-width, maximum lateral entry velocity and cheek throat adequacy are UNANSWERED.

STOP CONDITION (task section 14): the two instruments disagree above the plough threshold — the solver transports a centred ball at the envelope approach speed and Gazebo rejects it at the nip. Neither model was tuned to close the gap.
